open_points.subject: atomic replacement of the connections file
open_points.text: The agent replaces the file by writing a complete new file in the same folder and renaming it, so a reading sees the complete old file or the complete new one.
open_points.question: Who owns and enforces the atomic-replacement protocol: the external agent, object_connections, or another connection-record writer, given that object_connections owns the reading parts of A5 rule 7 but must not write connections?
options: The external agent owns the write protocol and object_connections assumes it.
object_connections must tolerate or reject non-atomic replacement while still never writing the file.
A separate connection-record writer owns atomic replacement and is a declared dependency of the agent.
open_points.default_guess: The external agent owns and tests atomic replacement; object_connections performs one ordinary read and assumes the writer contract.

witness.initial: A valid confirmed connections file is in use while the service is running.
events: The agent changes a connection while a scan reaches its connection check.
The scan reads while the new file is being installed.
outcomes: Atomic replacement is the agent's owned guarantee, so the scan sees the complete old or complete new file and continues from that reading.
The service-side reader owns protection against replacement details, so it detects, retries, snapshots, or refuses a concurrently exposed incomplete file.
witness.observer: The caller sees either a normal result from one complete record or a transient folder_unavailable/refusal.

open_points.subject: ObjectConnection invoice_subfolder containment
open_points.text: The deliverer never opens the invoice folder, so the resolved path of that folder is checked by the Cabinet Inbox when it moves to this record (R0-09).
open_points.question: Must an ObjectConnection whose invoice_subfolder resolves outside root be rejected now to satisfy M01's statement that both subfolders stay inside the root, or is such a record valid for the deliverer until the Cabinet Inbox later checks it?
options: Reject the whole connection record when either subfolder resolves outside root.
Validate only the requested project's photo folder in the deliverer; defer resolved invoice-folder containment to the Cabinet Inbox.
Treat resolved invoice containment as an agent-side precondition, without checking it in either current service.
open_points.default_guess: The deliverer validates only lexical invoice_subfolder form and defers its resolved containment to the Cabinet Inbox, while the model text is revised to distinguish a promised writer precondition from deliverer validation.

witness.initial: A confirmed record has a valid photo folder and an invoice_subfolder named invoices that is a symbolic link to a directory outside root.
events: The deliverer starts and receives an authenticated scan for the project.
outcomes: Under M01's statement that both subfolders stay inside root, the record is invalid and startup or loading refuses it with folder_unavailable.
Under A5 rule 8, startup does not resolve the invoice folder; the scan validates only the photo folder and proceeds.
witness.observer: The caller and service operator see whether the service accepts the record and performs the scan.
